extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners prosecuting U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards from the MPEP/CFR governing examination, applicant replies, amendments, suspensions/deferrals, citations, and evidentiary requirements during U.S. patent prosecution and reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action in a continued prosecution application (CPA) (§1.103(a)/(b) context)
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of the applicant, the Office may grant a suspension of action by the Office in a continued prosecution application filed under § 1.53(d) for a period not exceeding three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request must be filed with the request for an application filed under § 1.53(d), specify the period of suspension, and include the processing fee set forth in § 1.17(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited suspension of action after an RCE (§1.103(c) context)
rubrics_metrics.description: On request of the applicant, the Office may grant a suspension of action after filing a request for continued examination under § 1.114 for a period not exceeding three months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be filed with the RCE, specify period of suspension, and include processing fee set forth in § 1.17(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral of examination (§1.103(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: On request, the Office may grant a deferral of examination for a period not extending beyond three years from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is claimed under title 35 U.S.C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request must include the publication fee (§1.18(d)) and processing fee (§1.17(i)). A deferral will not be granted unless: (1) the application is an original utility or plant application filed under § 1.53(b) or resulting from national stage entry after § 1.495; (2) applicant has not filed a nonpublication request under § 1.213(a) (or has rescinded it under § 1.213(b)); (3) application is in condition for publication as provided in § 1.211(c); and (4) the Office has not issued an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 or a notice of allowance under 35 U.S.C. 151.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of action for public safety or defense (§1.103(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may suspend action by order of the Director if certain conditions are met regarding public safety or defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions: (1) application is owned by the United States; (2) publication may be detrimental to public safety or defense; (3) an appropriate department or agency requests such suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s duty to make a thorough study and investigation (§1.104(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application for examination or a patent in a reexamination proceeding, the examiner shall make a thorough study thereof and a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination must be complete as to compliance with statutes and rules and to the patentability of the invention as claimed, as well as matters of form, unless otherwise indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and statement of reasons in Office actions (§1.104(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant (or patent owner and requester in reexamination) will be notified of the examiner’s action; reasons for adverse action or any objection/requirement will be stated in an Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information or references will be given as may be useful in aiding the applicant/patent owner to judge propriety of continuing prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type search availability (§1.104(a)(3)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978; any national application may also have an international-type search report prepared upon written request and payment of fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal international-type search is not required to obtain a search fee refund in a later filed international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner’s action — permitted limitations (§1.104(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder of invention, fundamental defects), the action may be limited to such matters before further action is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters of form need not be raised by the examiner until a claim is found allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of claims when invention not patentable (§1.104(c)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not considered patentable, or not considered patentable as claimed, the claims, or those considered unpatentable will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to cite best references and explain pertinence for novelty/obviousness rejections (§1.104(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command; when a reference is complex or shows other inventions, the particular part relied on must be designated as nearly as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pertinence of each reference, if not apparent, must be clearly explained and each rejected claim specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and facts within examiner’s knowledge (§1.104(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant (or patent owner in reexamination) as to any matter affecting patentability and may rely upon facts within his or her knowledge pursuant to paragraph (d)(2) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of subject matter as commonly owned for 35 U.S.C. 102/103(c) purposes (§1.104(c)(4)-(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter that would otherwise qualify as prior art under certain 35 U.S.C. 102 provisions will be treated as commonly owned for purposes of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) or 103(c) if the applicant/patent owner provides specified statements (e.g., ownership or joint research agreement statements) and discloses or amends to disclose names of parties to agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed conditions: statements as to common ownership or joint research agreement (with timing and scope details) and disclosure/amendment to disclose names of parties are required. Special temporal rules apply for pre-/post-March 16, 2013 situations and specific filing date brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of references — data to be stated (§1.104(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the examiner cites references, various identifying information must be stated to enable identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic patents: numbers/dates/names of patentees. Domestic patent application publications: publication number, publication date, names of applicants. Foreign published applications/patents: nationality/country, numbers/dates, names of patentees, and other necessary data; identify particular pages/sheets if only part is relied on. Printed publications: author (if any), title, date, pages/plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejections based on facts within Office employee’s knowledge must be specific and supportable (§1.104(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection in an application is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an employee of the Office, the data shall be as specific as possible, and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such affidavit shall be subject to contradiction or explanation by affidavits of the applicant and other persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance — examiner explanation and applicant comment (§1.104(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes the record of prosecution does not make clear the reasons for allowing a claim, the examiner may set forth such reasoning in an Office action or separate communication; the applicant or patent owner may file a statement commenting on the reasons for allowance within a specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action or be the subject of a separate communication. Failure by the examiner to respond to any comment does not give rise to any implication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for information the examiner may request (§1.105(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: In examining/treating a matter, the examiner or other Office employee may require submission from individuals identified under § 1.56(c) or any assignee of such information as may be reasonably necessary to properly examine or treat the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: existence of relevant commercial databases; whether a prior art search was made and what was searched; copies of non-patent literature/published applications/patents by any inventor relating to the claimed invention; materials used to draft the application; materials used in the invention process; identification of what is improved where the invention is an improvement; identification of any use of the claimed invention known to any inventor at filing; technical information known to applicant concerning related art, disclosure, claimed subject matter, other factual information pertinent to patentability, or concerning accuracy of examiner’s interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted forms for requirements for factual information (§1.105(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for factual information may be presented in various manners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a requirement for factual information; interrogatories in the form of specific questions seeking applicant’s factual knowledge; stipulations as to facts with which the applicant may agree or disagree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of reply stating information is unknown or not readily available (§1.105(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply to a requirement for information that states the information required is unknown to or not readily available to the party from which it was requested may be accepted as a complete reply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of requirements for information (§1.105(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for information may be included in an Office action or sent separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to requirements for information governed by §§1.135 and 1.136 (§1.105(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply, or failure to reply, to a requirement for information under this section will be governed by the cited rule provisions concerning time and abandonment consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective filing date of a claimed invention (§1.109)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective filing date for a claimed invention (other than reissue) is the earliest of: (1) the actual filing date of the patent/application containing the claim; or (2) the filing date of the earliest application for which the patent/application is entitled to priority or benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119, 120, 121, 365, or 386.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue applications or reissued patents, the effective filing date for a claimed invention is determined by deeming the claim to have been contained in the patent for which reissue was sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require identification of inventorship and ownership of subject matter of individual claims (§1.110)
rubrics_metrics.description: When one or more joint inventors are named, the Office may require the applicant/patentee to identify inventorship and ownership or obligation to assign of each claimed invention on its effective filing date (or date of invention) when necessary for an Office proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may also require identification of invention dates of the subject matter of each claim when necessary for Office proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to a non-final Office action — must distinctly and specifically point out errors (§1.111(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To be entitled to reconsideration or further examination, the applicant/patent owner must reply in writing which distinctly and specifically points out the supposed errors in the examiner’s action and must reply to every ground of objection and rejection in the prior Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply must present arguments pointing out specific distinctions believed to render the claims patentable over applied references. A general allegation that the claims define a patentable invention without specifically pointing out how the language patentably distinguishes them does not comply. The reply must appear to be a bona fide attempt to advance the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental replies — limited entry as matter of right (§1.111(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply that is supplemental to a compliant reply will not be entered as a matter of right except as provided; the Office may enter a supplemental reply if it is clearly limited to certain topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted supplemental reply matters include: cancellation of claim(s); adoption of examiner suggestions; placement of the application in condition for allowance; reply to an Office requirement made after the first reply was filed; correction of informalities (e.g., typographical errors); simplification of issues for appeal. A supplemental reply will be entered if filed within a specified period during which action by the Office is suspended under § 1.103(a) or (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in reply must clearly point out patentable novelty (§1.111(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: In amending in reply to a rejection, the applicant or patent owner must clearly point out the patentable novelty believed to be present in the claims in view of the state of the art disclosed by cited references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must also show how the amendments avoid such references or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration before final action (§1.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a reply by applicant or patent owner to a non-final action, the application (or patent under reexamination) will be reconsidered and again examined; applicant/patent owner and third-party requester will be notified of rejections or favorable decisions in the same manner as after the first examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant/patent owner may reply in the same manner as provided in §1.111 unless the Office action indicates it is final, or an appeal has been taken, or certain reexamination closing actions have occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection or action — repetition of all grounds and statement of reasons (§1.113(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: On the second or any subsequent examination the rejection or other action may be made final; in making such final rejection the examiner shall repeat or state all grounds of rejection then considered applicable and clearly state reasons in support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply to a final rejection is limited to appeal or to amendment as specified in § 1.114 or § 1.116. Reply to a final rejection must include cancellation of, or appeal from, each rejected claim; if any claim stands allowed, reply must comply with any form requirements or objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for continued examination (RCE) timing and content (§1.114(a)-(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is closed, an applicant may request continued examination by filing a submission and the fee (§1.17(e)) prior to the earliest of: payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under §1.313 is granted); abandonment; or filing a notice of appeal to Fed. Cir. or commencement of a civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145/146 (unless terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution closed means application is under appeal, last Office action is final, a notice of allowance, or action that otherwise closes prosecution. A 'submission' includes IDS, amendment to specification/claims/drawings, new arguments, or new evidence. If timely filed, the Office will withdraw finality of any Office action and enter and consider the submission. Appeal/case briefs are not considered submissions. Section excludes provisional, certain pre-1995 applications, design applications, international design applications, and patents under reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary amendments — when part of original disclosure and entry (§1.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: A preliminary amendment received on or before the mail date of the first Office action under § 1.104: if present on the filing date it is part of the original disclosure; if filed after the filing date it is not part of the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A preliminary amendment in compliance with § 1.121 will be entered unless disapproved by the Director. A preliminary amendment seeking cancellation of all claims without presenting new/substitute claims will be disapproved. A preliminary amendment may be disapproved if it unduly interferes with preparation of the first Office action — factors include state of preparation of first Office action and nature of changes resulting. A preliminary amendment will not be disapproved if filed no later than: (i) three months from filing date of an application under §1.53(b); (ii) filing date of a continued prosecution application under §1.53(d); or (iii) three months from national stage entry under §1.491. Those time periods are not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and affidavits/evidence after final action and prior to appeal (§1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a final rejection/other final action but before or on the same date as filing an appeal or related dates, amendments may be admitted under specified conditions and affidavits or other evidence may be admitted upon showing good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and were not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: (1) amendment canceling claims or complying with form requirements; (2) amendment presenting rejected claims in better form for appeal may be admitted; (3) amendment touching merits may be admitted upon showing of good and sufficient reasons. Admission/refusal does not relieve application from its condition as subject to appeal or abandonment. Special limitations apply to inter partes reexamination and ex parte reexamination proceedings: e.g., in inter partes reexamination no amendment other than canceling claims (that do not affect scope of other pending claims) can be made after right of appeal notice except as provided in §1.981 or §41.77(b)(1). Similarly, affidavits/evidence in inter partes reexam after right of appeal notice generally cannot be made except as provided.
